name: Clostridioides difficile (C. diff)
short_description: Strictly anaerobic, S-layer-coated Gram-positive gut bacillus that grows as a long slender rod with peritrichous flagella and forms a swelling subterminal endospore, giving the classic club silhouette; when antibiotics thin the gut microbiota it overgrows the colon and its toxins TcdA and TcdB cause antibiotic-associated diarrhoea and pseudomembranous colitis.

textbook.1: reject: the muted palette, thin outlines and the three-layer Gram-positive envelope are all correct, and the spore is layered, but a frilled scallop-shell artefact is stuck on the upper-right pole and the spore sits right at the opposite tip rather than subterminally
textbook.2: reject: worse — the spore now caps the very end of the cell and a large grey spiky splash artefact hangs off that pole; the artefacts traced back to the word 'drumstick' in the prompt being read as a chicken drumstick with its paper frill, so the word was removed
textbook.3: accept: clean muted educational palette, thin outlines, dark charcoal ground full-bleed; the Gram-positive envelope is shown in section as exactly three layers (stippled slate-blue S-layer over a thick sage peptidoglycan wall over a violet plasma membrane) with no outer membrane and no LPS fringe; irregular blue-purple nucleoid tangle and teal ribosomes in a cream cytoplasm; the endospore is drawn in concentric shells (pale-gold core, sage cortex, laminated umber coat) and sits SUBTERMINALLY, with ordinary cell body continuing past it to the pole; peritrichous coral flagella from the sides and both ends; no text, no border, no artefacts. Knowing compromise: the rod is about three times longer than wide, at the stubby end of the documented 3-17 um range rather than the long slender ideal
textbook.4: reject: the elongation instruction worked and the rod is properly long and slim, but the spore moved back to cap the tip — the one do-NOT-draw item that matters most for this organism
textbook.5: reject: spore near-terminal again, the body is fat, and a strange cross-hatched 'cap' texture sits on the upper-left pole

sem.1: reject: handsome false-colour SEM with correct peritrichous flagella and a smooth S-layer surface, but the swelling is a terminal knob capping one end rather than a subterminal bulge, and the rod is only about four times longer than wide
sem.2: reject: the bulge over-corrected all the way to mid-cell — a centrally-placed spore is an explicit do-NOT-draw item — and ballooned to several times the shaft width, so the cell reads as a nematode rather than a bacillus
sem.3: accept: long slender butter-gold rod on a clean teal-grey substrate; the swelling sits about a third of the way in from one pole with a clear length of ordinary slim rod continuing past it to a rounded pole, giving exactly the subterminal club silhouette the reference describes; surface-only detail, as SEM should be, with the endospore revealed only as the outward bulge; peritrichous flagella springing from the sides and both ends; no text, scale bar, border or second specimen

3d.1: reject: near-monochrome — the whole cell body is one flat sage green — with a pronounced background vignette, and the flagella are bunched at two spots rather than peritrichous
3d.2: reject (near miss): the spore is correctly subterminal and the tints are acceptable, but the background still carries a strong vignette and the cutaway is a narrow rectangular slot that hides the envelope layering
3d.3: reject: the spore caps the lower-left tip and the body is only about four times longer than wide
3d.4: reject: same terminal-spore failure, the spore forming the end cap of the cell
3d.5: accept: long slim rod on a seamless near-black ground with no vignette; the spore sits clearly SUBTERMINAL with slim rod on both sides of it and a rounded pole beyond; concentric pale-gold core, sage cortex and laminated umber coat; three-layer Gram-positive envelope (grey-blue S-layer skin, thick sage wall, violet plasma membrane) over an amber cytoplasm with a blue-purple nucleoid tangle and teal ribosomes; many coral flagella distributed peritrichously; natural biological tints throughout, not near-monochrome and not neon; no text, no border

watercolor.1: reject: the full-bleed aged paper is right, but a grey shredded tassel artefact hangs off the upper-right tip and the spore caps that same tip
watercolor.2: reject: same tassel artefact, spore still terminal, and the rod has thinned to a matchstick with the spore ballooning out of proportion
watercolor.3: accept: warm aged paper filling the frame corner to corner with a soft wash halo painted directly on it (no sheet, mat, border, margin or deckled edge); slim rod with the endospore set clearly inboard from the upper-right pole and ordinary rod continuing past it to the rounded pole; concentric pale-gold core, sage cortex and laminated umber coat; stippled slate-blue S-layer over a sage wall over a violet membrane, cream cytoplasm, blue-purple nucleoid tangle, teal ribosomes; fine coral peritrichous flagella in ink and wash; no text, no border, no artefacts

reference: accept: CDC PHIL #6260 (Public Domain, PD-USGov-HHS-CDC, CDC / Lois S. Wiggs, 2004), a scanning electron micrograph of Clostridioides difficile recovered from a stool specimen, taken at 3006x. Native resolution is 2835 x 1927 px — genuinely high-resolution, nothing was upscaled. The download (real-01) is greyscale, carries the instrument data band and 10 um scale bar across the bottom, and shows two dense clumps of rods. The edit_image.py clean-up (real-02, gemini-3-pro-image) removed the data band, isolated two individual rods from the sparse periphery of the field and applied a natural false colour (butter-gold cells on a cool teal-grey substrate), since the original is greyscale. It unambiguously shows the organism: long, gently curved rods with blunt rounded poles and the smooth S-layer-covered surface. TWO HONEST CAVEATS. (1) real-02 is a model-mediated recomposition, not a plain crop: the outlines and surface relief come from the PD original but the isolation, background and false colour were generated. (2) Neither flagella nor a spore-swollen cell are resolved in this particular field, so the reference documents proportions, poles and surface texture — not the endospore. The un-edited download is kept as real-01 for provenance.
decision: gen-03__gemini-3-pro-image — the primary teaching figure and the svg_theme: the cleanest statement of the Gram-positive three-layer envelope plus the layered subterminal endospore. Base for labels.json.

gen-03__gemini-3-pro-image — the best silhouette in the set: long slim rod with the swelling set clearly back from the pole. Deliberately left unlabelled; SEM shows surface only, and its teaching value here is the bare club outline next to the real micrograph.
gen-05__gemini-3-pro-image — took five passes to get the spore off the tip while keeping natural biological tints and a vignette-free background.
gen-03__gemini-3-pro-image — full-bleed paper, subterminal spore, legible spore layering, first pass on the Pro model.
notes: Model ladder: attempts 1-2 of every style on gemini-2.5-flash-image, attempts 3+ on gemini-3-pro-image. Flash failed the same way on all four styles at once — it put the endospore at the tip (or, over-correcting, dead-centre) and added frilled shell/tassel artefacts at the pole — which traced to the word 'drumstick' in the prompt being read as a chicken drumstick with its paper frill; removing the word and specifying the spore's position numerically (segments 3-5 of ten along the rod) fixed it on the Pro model. KNOWN COMPROMISES, flagged honestly: (a) the chosen textbook render is only about 3x longer than wide, at the stubby end of the documented 3.0-16.9 um x 0.5-1.9 um range — the two attempts that got the elongation right both put the spore back on the tip, and a correct spore was judged worth more than correct proportions; the sem, 3d and watercolor renders all carry the long slender proportions. (b) The exosporium is described in the science section but not given its own leader line: at this scale the generated art does not reliably separate it from the outer coat. (c) In all four styles the spore is drawn conspicuously large relative to the mother cell so its concentric layers are legible; in reality it is a tighter fit. (d) The watercolor's soft wash halo reads slightly as a cast drop-shadow rather than a flat wash, though it sits on the paper and there is no sheet, mat or border. (e) None of the styles show gut-lumen context props — deliberately, since the style rules require an uncluttered background for label legibility; the gut setting is carried by the coloring page and the descriptions instead.
